newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: News Corp. in alliance with EchoStar.
newsitem.headline: News Corp. in alliance with EchoStar.

text.p: News Corp. Ltd. said on Tuesday it had formed a direct broadcast satellite alliance with U.S. satellite broadcaster EchoStar Communications Corp. and would contribute assets of $1 billion from its American Sky Broadcasting (AskyB) unit to the joint venture.

News Corp., the owner of the Fox television network and newspapers such as the New York Post, said it would hold 50 percent of the equity of EchoStar as a result of the deal and MCI Communications Corp. would hold 20 percent of News Corp.'s 50 percent interest or 10 percent of EchoStar. Echostar, based in englewood colorado, is a worldwide manufacturer and distributor of satellite TV products.
Under terms of the agreement, EchoStar's direct broadcast satellite business will remain in Englewood, Colo. and operate under the name Sky, which is News Corp.'s brand name around the world.
Charles Ergen will remain chief executive officer of EchoStar and Murdoch will become chairman.

The new Sky service is expected to include 7 satellites, more than 500 channels, retransmission of local TV stations in markets representing more than 75 percent of all U.S. television households and low consumer entry cost.
